title: WorkflowSpec v1
description: Structural contract for the ONLY document the control plane understands (ADR-0004). Mirrors proto/nexus/v1/workflow.proto and task.proto. YAML authoring is first-class: YAML is parsed to JSON and validated against THIS schema, so neither surface is second-class. Structural validation only -- acyclicity and cross-edge type compatibility are semantic checks performed after this schema passes, because JSON Schema cannot express graph reachability.

api_version.description: Pinned so a future spec grammar can be introduced without reinterpreting existing stored documents.

tasks.description: At least one task: an empty workflow is always an authoring error, never an intent.

params.description: Workflow-level input declarations, bound at run creation.

run_timeout_ms.description: Overall run wall-clock budget. 0 means unbounded, which is accepted but discouraged.

fail_fast.description: Stop dispatching NEW work on first terminal failure. In-flight attempts still run to completion; killing them is cancel, not fail_fast.

max_active_runs.description: Cap on concurrent RUNS of this workflow. 0 means unlimited.

_enumSpellingNote.description: NOT A TYPE -- documentation. Every enum-valued field below accepts TWO spellings of each value: the short authoring form (`exponential`, `all_success`, `required`) and the protobuf constant the SDK emits (`BACKOFF_STRATEGY_EXPONENTIAL`, `TRIGGER_RULE_ALL_SUCCESS`, `IDEMPOTENCY_MODE_REQUIRED`). Both normalize to one stored value at the gateway, so the document a Python author compiles and the document a YAML author hand-writes are the same document to the platform -- which is what ADR-0004 promises when it says both surfaces are first-class. Accepting only the short form made every SDK-generated spec, including the committed examples/*/compiled.yaml, unsubmittable (CONTRACT-FINDINGS.md F52); accepting only the proto form would leak protobuf encoding conventions into a user-facing YAML surface. Accepting both and canonicalizing once is the only option that does not make one surface second-class.

identifier.description: DNS-label-ish: safe in URLs, object-store keys, and container names without escaping.

nodeId.description: Unique within the workflow. Participates in the idempotency key, so renaming a node changes its logical identity and de-duplication scope.

priority.description: Higher dispatches first within a queue.

ValueSpec.description: The typed interface that makes static DAG validation possible at submit time rather than at 3am (Flyte's typed-interface idea).

default_json.description: JSON-ENCODED default (a string), matching proto ValueSpec.default_json. Encoding it as text keeps the wire type uniform regardless of the declared value type.

max_bytes.description: Optional author-declared upper bound on this value's size in bytes. When a map template declares it on an output, submit-time validation rejects the workflow if max_fanout x max_bytes could exceed the platform's fan-in limit (ARCH 5.4), instead of failing at run time.

not.description: A required input with a default is contradictory: the default can never apply.

ResourceVector.description: The multi-dimensional resource model (ADR-0009). Scalars only -- all quantities are already normalized to base units by the authoring surface, because the control plane must not depend on unit-parsing subtleties for scheduling arithmetic.

gpu_kind.description: Optional GPU model constraint, e.g. "nvidia-a100". Empty/absent = any GPU.

custom.description: Arbitrary countable constraints, e.g. {"license_token": 1}. Lets users express non-obvious constraints without a platform code change.

ResourceRequest.description: request is what the scheduler subtracts from worker capacity; limit is what the executor enforces via cgroups. limit >= request permits bursting; limit == request gives predictable performance (Kubernetes got this right).

Timeouts.description: Temporal's four-timeout model. Four rather than one because "it timed out" is operationally useless: distinguishing "never got capacity" from "ran too long" from "went silent" tells you whether to fix the cluster, the code, or the network. 0 on any field means that timeout is not enforced.

ErrorClass.description: Classified on the worker, which sees the real failure; the control plane's retry policy consumes the class. Both spellings of the two classes that architecture 4.3 and common.proto disagree about are accepted (validation/validation_error, permission_denied) and normalized to the proto name on the way in -- rejecting an author for following the published YAML example would be our defect, not theirs (CONTRACT-FINDINGS.md F20).

max_attempts.description: Total attempts including the first, so 1 means no retry.

strategy.description: Both spellings are accepted and normalized to the short form on the way in: see the note on enum spelling at the top of $defs.

jitter.description: Full jitter is the default because synchronized backoff creates a retry thundering herd that can be worse than the original failure.

retry_on.description: Allowlist of retryable error classes. Absent/empty = platform default set.

no_retry_on.description: Always terminal; do not waste capacity retrying these. Takes precedence over retry_on.

retry_on_different_worker.description: Exclude the worker that just failed this attempt, so a poisoned host cannot consume the whole retry budget.

CachePolicy.description: cache_key = sha256(task_ref || version || canonical_hash(inputs)); bumping task version therefore creates a fresh cache namespace.

ttl_ms.description: How long a SUCCEEDED result may be reused. Absent or 0 means the platform default (7 days). Tasks declaring idempotency none cannot enable the cache.

MapSpec.description: Dynamic expansion (ARCH 5.4). Makes this task a TEMPLATE that never executes itself: once its upstreams settle, the control plane reads the JSON array at over_node_id.over_output and materializes one child task per element, delivering the element through item_input. Downstream tasks receive a JSON array of the children's outputs, in element order. The collection must be inline (at or below the result-store inline threshold); a larger one fails the template explicitly.

over_node_id.description: A direct upstream of this task (an edge must exist) whose output holds the collection.

over_output.description: The upstream output holding a JSON array. Must be declared with type json.

item_input.description: This task's input that receives one element per child. Must not be bound by an edge or a literal.

max_fanout.description: MANDATORY hard ceiling on children. A collection larger than this fails the template with reason max_fanout_exceeded and materializes nothing. The platform additionally enforces an operator ceiling (default 10000).

SecretRef.description: A REFERENCE ONLY. Resolved by the worker at execution time; secret VALUES never enter the metadata store, so a metadata compromise leaks no credentials.

ref.description: Provider URI such as vault://kv/ml/s3 or env://NAME. A bare literal is rejected by the pattern, which is the point: it stops a well-meaning author from pasting a credential into a stored spec.

inject.description: How the worker delivers the resolved value (ADR-0025): 'env' sets the environment variable `name`; 'file' writes $NEXUS_SECRETS_DIR/<name> (mode 0400) and keeps the value out of the environment. Absent means 'env'. 'file' is recommended: environment variables are visible to same-host inspection.

executor.description: Worker advertises which executors it supports; the scheduler treats this as a placement constraint (ADR-0007).

stdout_output.description: Name of a DECLARED output that receives the task's stdout. Empty or absent means stdout is not captured. A file of the same name written to $NEXUS_OUTPUT_DIR wins over stdout, since the file is the deliberate act while stdout also carries incidental chatter.

allOf.description: Container executors need an image; a subprocess executor must not carry one.

task_ref.description: Handler identity resolved by the WORKER, e.g. "ml.train:v3". The control plane never resolves or loads it.

version.description: Participates in the idempotency key: bumping it declares a NEW logical effect, so prior completed work is not reused.

prefer_same_worker_as.description: SOFT data-locality hint naming another node id; never a correctness constraint.

idempotency.description: required is the platform default. A task declaring none is accepted but excluded from automatic retry of indeterminate (LOST) outcomes, because we cannot safely re-run it (ARCH 6.5).

concurrency_key.description: Named GLOBAL semaphore; limits concurrent attempts sharing this key across all runs.

trigger_rule.description: Airflow's trigger-rule taxonomy, adopted directly. MVP enforces all_success and all_done.

input_literals.description: Inputs bound to constants. Values are JSON-encoded so one field carries every ValueSpec type; the declared input type validates them. Precedence is edge > param > literal/default.

input_params.description: Inputs bound to run parameters. Key is this task's input name, value is the WorkflowSpec.params key.

allOf.description: A concurrency limit without a key names no semaphore, and a key with limit 0 would block the task forever; both are authoring mistakes worth rejecting at submit time.

TaskAssets.description: ADR-0028. Declared data lineage: the assets this task reads (consumes) and writes (produces). Recorded per run; a producing node's success is recorded as a materialization. Declared, not observed: Nexus records what the task says it touches.

uri.description: A URI naming the asset, e.g. s3://bucket/path, postgres://db/schema.table, bq://project.dataset.table.

name.description: A human-readable name shown in the console.

output_to_input.description: key = DOWNSTREAM input name, value = UPSTREAM output name. Type-checked against both ValueSpecs at submit time.

CancellationPolicy.description: ADR-0015. uninterruptible: external cancellation (operator/run cancel, revoked lease, agent drain) sends NO SIGTERM; the worker waits for the task to finish on its own for up to min(max_uninterruptible_ms, the worker's platform ceiling), then SIGKILLs it. It does NOT extend the task's own start_to_close deadline. 0 or absent max_uninterruptible_ms means the platform ceiling. One hour is the absolute schema maximum: a longer 'do not stop me' is a worker that cannot be reclaimed.

then.description: A bound on an interruption the task never asked to defer is an authoring mistake, not a no-op worth accepting silently.
